overview.text: The Georgian icon tradition centres on an image taken from Georgia to Persia and later brought to Krasnogorsk. It includes a number of separately venerated copies.

blocks.text: Kirill Ulanov’s 1707 panel shows the Mother of God holding Christ and turning her free hand toward Him. The Child’s exposed leg and compact seated posture are visible. The file identifies Ulanov and the Tretyakov setting; this dated Russian work is not presented as the earlier image brought from Persia.

blocks.text: The OCA recounts Stephen Lazarev’s purchase and Gregory Lytkin’s direction of the icon to the Pinega region in 1629. It associates August 22 with its arrival at the monastery and describes subsequent investigations and later Moscow copies. It also distinguishes the Alekseev Convent image from the Krasnogorsk and Nikitniki examples.

blocks.text: The Tatarstan Metropolia’s Raifa history identifies its principal shrine as a faithful copy of the Krasnogorsk Georgian image. It connects that copy with Metropolitan Lavrenty’s commission and a specially sent icon-painter. That local history concerns the Raifa copy, not Ulanov’s 1707 panel or an assertion that every Georgian-named icon is the Athonite Iveron original.
